<reason>Side A (CON) built a stronger path to victory by exposing the logistical infeasibility of a home-first default under caregiver scarcity. They effectively attacked the "when possible" clause, arguing it creates a reactive system where elders transition only after crises. In the decisive Rebuttal 2, Side A caught Side B in a direct contradiction—dismissing 24/7 staffing as a strawman while simultaneously promising overnight aides—undermining the feasibility of the home-care proposal. Side B mounted a compelling ethical case for autonomy and burden of proof but failed to adequately resolve the resource constraints and scalability issues, leaving their case vulnerable on the proposition's core "when possible" condition.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side A's Rebuttal 2 (A1), which exposed Side B's contradiction between dismissing 24/7 continuous staffing as a "strawman" in the Pressure Questions round and then promising "overnight aides" and "24/7 support" in Rebuttal 2, thereby revealing the shell game behind the "when possible" standard and damaging Side B's live route to victory on feasibility.</best_rebuttal>
